activities.anchor: Three threshold questions can end a case before anyone hears its substance
activities.caption: pair each gate with what it demands
activities.name: cmGatesMatch

config.prompt: The gates before the merits — pair each with what it demands:

pairs.right: power over this subject matter, this territory, this defendant — or dismissal however meritorious
the Limitation Act 1980: contract and tort six years, personal injury three, defamation one
the right claimant — the person whose right is at stake
"promptly, and in any event within three months"

config.why: Procedural rules look technical precisely because they are the law's way of refusing stale, misdirected or meddlesome claims — and every gate is also a trap that has killed real cases.

activities.anchor: Civil litigation in England and Wales runs on the Civil Procedure Rules
activities.caption: line up the civil pipeline as Woolf designed it
activities.name: cmCivilOrder

config.prompt: Judicial case management, stage by stage — order the pipeline:
items: pre-action protocols — letters and documents exchanged before suing
claim form and particulars of claim issued
allocation to a track by value and complexity (small claims, fast, multi)
disclosure, witness statements, expert reports — the longest, most decisive phase
trial — a judge alone, on the balance of probabilities
config.why: Disclosure clears the fog and settlement follows — the system working, since a trial is the most expensive way to resolve anything. And costs usually follow the event: the loser pays most of the winner's costs, the pressure shaping every tactical decision upstream.

config.root: The defendant puts a sealed offer of 50,000 on the table under CPR Part 36. You are the claimant; your adviser privately prices the case at 60,000. Trial comes.

choices.label: Reject the offer — and beat it at trial
choices.feedback: The claimant collects extra costs and enhanced interest: the arithmetic rewarded your self-assessment.

choices.label: Reject the offer — and fail to beat it at trial
choices.feedback: You pay extra costs and enhanced interest: refusing the better price was expensive.

choices.label: Accept the 50,000
choices.feedback: Guaranteed money, no trial risk — the offer's pull is the point.

win.text: You beat your own price. The sealed offer becomes the defendant's problem.

choices.label: See what failing would have cost
choices.feedback: Symmetry: the same rule punishes the other direction.

lose.text: The offer you refused was the better deal. Guessing wrong is expensive by design.

choices.label: See the winning side of the rule

settle.text: Certainty beats the gamble. A large share of cases close the day after an offer expires.

config.why: The rule weaponises information and self-assessment: each side must privately price its case, and the abstract encouragement to settle becomes arithmetic.

activities.anchor: The venue decision follows the offence class
activities.caption: file each offence class by its venue
activities.name: cmVenueBuckets

config.prompt: Venue follows the offence class — file each:

items.label: either-way, defendant picks the faster route (sentence capped at 12 months)
either-way, elected up for a jury and unlimited sentence
conviction by unanimity or a 10–2 majority (Juries Act 1974)
roughly 95 per cent of criminal cases

config.why: A guilty plea short-circuits everything at the first hearing — earning a sentencing discount of up to a third, the system's main lubricant.

activities.anchor: The appellate structure is a filter pyramid
activities.caption: true or false — what each rung reviews
activities.name: cmAppealJudge

statements.s: Appeal courts re-hear the witnesses so they can check the facts themselves.
statements.why: They correct errors of law and procedure and check verdicts are "safe" — the trial judge saw the witnesses; the appellate court reads a transcript.

statements.s: From the Crown Court, appeal lies to the Court of Appeal (Criminal Division) — but only with leave, where the conviction is "unsafe".
statements.why: The Criminal Appeal Act 1995 widened this to fresh evidence; the Criminal Cases Review Commission (created 1997) sends possibly-wrong convictions back.

statements.s: From the magistrates' court a defendant may appeal to the Crown Court as a full rehearing, or by "case stated" to the High Court on a point of law.
statements.why: Two different rungs for two different complaints — facts or law.

statements.s: A Supreme Court ruling becomes the binding rule the next thousand cases inherit — which is why leave is granted in only a small minority of applications.
statements.why: The final rung converts case into precedent: the system rations its precedent-making capacity. (The Supreme Court itself dates from the Constitutional Reform Act 2005, sitting since 2009.)

activities.anchor: The map is staffed by a distinctive division of labour
activities.caption: pair each role with its job
activities.name: cmPersonnelMatch

config.prompt: Who actually runs the system — pair the role with its job:

pairs.right: advise clients, draft documents, run cases day to day
specialist advocates instructed for court — the specialist bar still dominates the Crown Court and above
appointed since 2006 through the independent Judicial Appointments Commission, ending the "secret garden"
volunteers deciding the bulk of criminal cases
decide the serious ones — justice done by the community, not only by professionals

config.why: Judicial independence is the load-bearing wall: paid from the Consolidated Fund, tenure protected, removal only by address in Parliament — and the Miller judgments show the modern court pushing back on executive power.

activities.anchor: Procedure is worthless if you cannot afford to use it
activities.caption: drag the divider — the funded track and the cut one
activities.name: cmFundingCompare

config.prompt: Two tracks, two funding stories — drag the divider:

before.label: Criminal legal aid — survives
before.text: The state pays for defence representation, means-tested, on the theory that it cannot prosecute someone it has also deprived of counsel.

after.label: Civil legal aid — cut by LASPO 2012
after.text: Removed for most family, housing, welfare-benefit and immigration disputes; the vacuum filled by "no win, no fee" agreements and after-the-event insurance — which work for strong money claims, not for benefits appeals or eviction defences.

config.why: The measured result: a collapse in legal-aid-funded civil cases and a surge in litigants in person — people arguing their own cases before judges built for a two-sided contest. Funding decisions decide the real caseload, whatever the rules say on paper.

activities.anchor: The ceremony follows a fixed script designed for fairness
activities.caption: stage the trial day in order
activities.name: cmTrialOrder

config.prompt: The trial's fixed script — order it:
items: counsel open with short speeches stating what they intend to prove
claimant's evidence — witnesses cross-examined, then re-examined
the judge's summing-up: the law and the rival facts, set out neutrally
config.why: In the Crown Court the prosecutor opens first and carries the burden throughout; the defendant may stay silent — though adverse inferences may now be drawn (Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994). English judges control questioning and steer pace: advocacy as a chess game of precise questions, not monologues.
